newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian airforce men cleared in school deaths.
newsitem.headline: Italian airforce men cleared in school deaths.

text.p: Three Italian air force officers whose crashing aircraft killed 12 students in a school were acquitted by an appeal court on Wednesday of manslaughter.

The appeal court in the central city of Bologna, near where the disaster occurred in December 1990, ruled that no crime had been committed and quashed convictions from the previous trial, which had sentenced the three men to 30 months in jail.
Lawyers for relatives of the dead and for some of the 90 people injured in the crash said they would appeal further to Italy's highest court, the Court of Cassation.
The crash involved an Italian Macchi MB326 that had taken off from Villafranca airbase near the northern city of Verona during a military exercise.

The aircraft ran into engine problems and the pilot was unable to make an emergency landing at Bologna's airport. He ejected after pointing the plane at an uninhabited hillside but the pilotless aircraft changed direction and hit the school.
The defendants were the pilot, Captain Bruno Viviani, and two of his superior officers at the time, Eugenio Brega and Roberto Corsini, both colonels.
